name: Inside the City Walls (Beilin)
tagline: Bell Tower, Muslim Quarter and old lanes
description: The historic core enclosed by Xi'an's intact Ming walls, centred on the Bell and Drum Towers, with the Muslim Quarter food lanes on one side and quiet grey-brick hutong-style alleys on the other. Two metro lines cross here. Nowhere else in the city is this walkable or this atmospheric.
bestFor: Short-stay nomads who want history outside the window and everything on foot.
pros: Metro Lines 1 and 2 interchange at the Bell Tower
You can cycle the full circuit of the city wall
Endless cheap street food in the Muslim Quarter
cons: Constant tour groups around the Bell Tower
Older buildings, thin walls and street noise
Winter air quality in the basin is genuinely bad

name: Xiaozhai
description: The junction south of the walls where several universities meet a cluster of malls, cinemas and underground shopping streets. Cheap noodle shops, milk tea counters and budget chain hotels line the roads, and the Big Wild Goose Pagoda sits a short walk east. Busy, young and priced for students.
bestFor: Budget nomads who want cheap rent, cheap food and a metro stop.
pros: Cheapest decent rooms near the metro
Excellent value food at all hours
Line 2 and Line 3 both serve the area
cons: Noisy and short on quiet places to work

name: Gaoxin (High-Tech Zone)
description: The western high-tech zone along Gaoxin Road and Keji Road, where Xi'an's software firms, multinationals and better hotels concentrate. Modern serviced apartments, specialty coffee, international schools and a couple of decent hospitals sit within a few blocks. This is where most working foreigners in Xi'an end up.
bestFor: Remote workers who want new-build apartments, real coffee and reliable services.
pros: Newest apartment stock with lifts and heating
Best specialty cafes and coworking in the city
cons: Wide roads and long blocks make it tiring to walk
Roughly 30 minutes from the historic centre

name: Qujiang New District
description: A planned southeastern district built around Tang Paradise, the Datang Everbright City night street and the Big Wild Goose Pagoda park, with lakes, museums and wide landscaped boulevards. Housing is newer and lower density than the centre, and families dominate. Line 3 and Line 5 connect it back into town.
bestFor: Nomads who want quiet, clean streets and parks to run in after work.
pros: Lots of green space, lakes and museums
New, well-built apartments at fair prices
The best night walking street in the city
cons: The Tang-themed areas get heavily touristed
Spread out, you rely on the metro or taxis
Thin on independent cafes away from the attractions

name: Weiyang & North Station
tagline: Newer northern grid by the high-speed rail
description: The northern administrative district around Xi'an North Railway Station and the Daming Palace ruins park, all new towers, wide avenues and metro Line 2 running straight south into the walls. Rents undercut Gaoxin and Qujiang substantially, and the high-speed rail hub is a few minutes away.
bestFor: Nomads who travel by rail often and want cheap, modern space to come home to.
pros: Cheap modern apartments with good light
High-speed rail station on the doorstep
Daming Palace park for running and cycling
cons: Sterile new-build streets with little atmosphere
Around 25 minutes by metro to the old city
Dust from ongoing construction, worse in spring
